## 1. Overview & Profile

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| Official Name | Saudi Exchange (formerly Saudi Stock Exchange, Tadawul) |
| Abbreviation | Tadawul |
| Website | https://www.saudiexchange.sa |
| Year Established | 2007 (formal incorporation as joint stock company; electronic trading since 2001; informal stock trading since 1954) |
| Country / City | Saudi Arabia / Riyadh (King Fahd Road) |
| Ownership Structure | Publicly listed on its own exchange (ticker: 1111) since December 2021; PIF retains 70% |
| Parent Company / Group | Saudi Tadawul Group Holding Company (listed December 8, 2021 at SAR 105/share; market cap SAR 12.6B at IPO) |
| Regulatory Authority | Capital Market Authority (CMA), established 2003 under the Capital Market Law |
| Market Capitalization (listed companies) | ~SAR 10+ trillion (~USD 2.7 trillion) as of early 2026; largest exchange in the Middle East |
| Total Listed Instruments | ~390+ companies (Main Market ~230+ and Nomu ~80+), plus ETFs, REITs, sukuk/bonds |
| Average Daily Trading Value | SAR 4.59 billion (USD 1.22 billion) for February 2026 |
| Average Daily Trading Volume | [unverified â specific share volume data not confirmed for 2026] |

### Key Historical Milestones
- 1954: Informal share trading begins in Saudi Arabia
- 1984: Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) begins regulating the stock market; Saudi Share Registration Company (SSRC) established
- 2001: Launch of Tadawul electronic trading, clearing, and settlement system (October 16), replacing manual processes
- 2003: Capital Market Authority (CMA) established under the Capital Market Law (Royal Decree No. M/30)
- 2007: Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) formally incorporated as a joint stock company on March 19, authorized as the sole securities exchange in Saudi Arabia
- 2008: Tadawul begins using Nasdaq OMX's SAXESS trading platform
- 2015: Qualified Foreign Investor (QFI) program launched, opening direct market access to institutional foreign investors for the first time; Saudi Tadawul Group IPO strategy initiated
- 2015: X-Stream INET trading platform launched (September 13), replacing SAXESS â first in the Middle East to adopt Nasdaq's fastest trading engine
- 2017: Nomu â Parallel Market launched (February 26) for SME listings with lighter requirements
- 2018: QFI eligibility thresholds lowered; per-investor ownership cap raised from 5% to 10%
- 2019: Saudi Aramco IPO (December 11) â raised USD 25.6 billion, the world's largest IPO; Aramco reached ~USD 1.88 trillion market cap on debut, becoming the world's most valuable listed company
- 2019: MSCI Emerging Market and FTSE Russell EM index inclusion completed (phased from May-August for MSCI, March-December for FTSE Russell), catalyzing major foreign capital inflows
- 2020: Closing Auction and Trade-at-Last session introduced; settlement cycle changed to T+2; trading hours updated
- 2020: Volatility interruption mechanism introduced for newly listed securities (Main Market) and all Nomu securities
- 2021: Saudi Tadawul Group restructured into holding company with four subsidiaries and listed on its own exchange (December 8); IPO 121x oversubscribed by institutions
- 2023: Derivatives market developments including SF30 Futures Index; GCC Exchanges Committee (chaired by Tadawul) introduced 29 Unified ESG Metrics
- 2025: Record IPO activity â 38 company listings (13 on TASI, 24 on Nomu, plus 1 ETF); tick size reform effective June 29
- 2026: QFI regime abolished; market opened to all categories of foreign investors with barrier-free direct access from February 1, 2026

### Strategic Significance â Vision 2030

Saudi Exchange is a cornerstone of **Saudi Vision 2030** and the **Financial Sector Development Program (FSDP)**. Key alignment areas include:
- **Diversification from oil**: The Aramco IPO was designed to raise capital for non-oil economic diversification
- **Capital market deepening**: New products (derivatives, sukuk, REITs, ETFs), market segments (Nomu), and progressive foreign investor liberalization
- **Global index inclusion**: MSCI and FTSE Russell EM inclusion (2019) created a virtuous cycle of visibility, foreign flows, and institutional development
- **Private sector growth**: Nomu parallel market supports SME access to capital, aligning with Vision 2030's goal of increasing SME contribution to GDP

## 2. Market Structure

### 2.1 Market Segments

| Segment | Description | Listing Requirements (Summary) |
|---------|-------------|-------------------------------|
| **Main Market (TASI)** | Primary market for large and mid-cap companies; home to blue-chip names including Saudi Aramco, SABIC, Al Rajhi Bank; tracked by the Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) | Minimum market cap SAR 300 million; 3-year operating track record; 30% minimum free float (or 20% if market cap > SAR 2 billion); CMA-approved prospectus; profitability and corporate governance requirements |
| **Nomu â Parallel Market** | Growth market for SMEs with lighter listing requirements; accessible only to qualified investors (institutional and high-net-worth individuals) | Minimum market cap SAR 10 million; minimum 20% free float; no profitability track record required; must appoint a financial advisor; 1-year operating track record |

**Additional Segments:**
- **Sukuk and Bonds Market**: Trading of fixed-income instruments including government sukuk and corporate bonds
- **ETFs and Mutual Funds**: Listed exchange-traded funds and closed-ended investment funds
- **REITs**: Listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (introduced 2016)

### 2.2 Trading Sessions

**Note:** Saudi Arabia uses Arabia Standard Time (AST, UTC+3) year-round (no daylight saving time). The trading week is **Sunday to Thursday** (Friday and Saturday are the weekend).

**Normal Trading Day**

| Session | Local Time (AST) | UTC | Description |
|---------|------------------|-----|-------------|
| Pre-Open | 09:30 - 10:00 | 06:30 - 07:00 | Orders can be entered, amended, cancelled; no matching; indicative prices displayed |
| Opening Auction | 10:00:00 - 10:00:30 | 07:00:00 - 07:00:30 | Random uncross within 30-second window determines opening price |
| Continuous Trading | 10:00 - 15:00 | 07:00 - 12:00 | Continuous order matching by price-time priority |
| Pre-Close | 15:00 - 15:10 | 12:00 - 12:10 | Closing auction order accumulation period |
| Closing Auction Uncross | 15:10:00 - 15:10:30 | 12:10:00 - 12:10:30 | Random uncross within 30-second window determines closing price |
| Trade-at-Last | 15:10 - 15:20 | 12:10 - 12:20 | Trading permitted only at the closing auction price |

- **Total Continuous Trading:** 5 hours per day (10:00-15:00 AST)
- **No lunch break** (unlike many Asian exchanges)
- **Randomized open/close:** Both opening and closing auction uncross times are randomized within a 30-second window to enhance market integrity

### 2.3 Tick Sizes

**Equity Tick Size Bands (effective June 29, 2025)**

| Price Range (SAR) | Tick Size (SAR) |
|-------------------|-----------------|
| Below 25.00 | 0.01 |
| 25.00 - 49.98 | 0.02 |
| 50.00 - 99.95 | 0.05 |
| 100.00 - 249.90 | 0.10 |
| 250.00 - 499.75 | 0.25 |
| 500.00 and above | 0.50 |

The June 2025 reform lowered the minimum tick for sub-SAR 25 securities from SAR 0.02 to SAR 0.01, and introduced new bands for higher-priced securities. The reform applies to both Main Market and Nomu, excluding debt instruments.

*Source: [Saudi Exchange announcement, June 26, 2025](https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/the-saudi-exchange-amends-tick-size-bands-of-securities-to-enhance-market-effici-2025626); [Sahm Capital](https://www.sahmcapital.com/support/detail/tick-size-changes-in-the-saudi-stock-market)*

### 2.4 Lot Sizes
- **Standard lot:** 1 share (minimum tradeable quantity is 1 share) [unverified â some sources indicate odd lot trading availability; confirm with official rules]
- **Odd lot trading:** Available

### 2.5 Market Maker / Liquidity Provider Programs
- Saudi Exchange operates a market-making framework to enhance liquidity for listed securities
- Market makers are licensed by CMA and provide continuous two-sided quotes
- Coverage includes equities, ETFs, and derivatives [unverified â detailed programme terms not confirmed]

## 3. Trading Mechanism

### 3.1 Auction Mechanisms

- **Opening Auction:** During the Pre-Open phase (09:30-10:00 AST), orders accumulate without matching. The system displays indicative opening prices. At 10:00, a randomized uncross occurs within a 30-second window (10:00:00-10:00:30), determining the opening price via a single-price auction that maximizes executable volume.

- **Closing Auction:** The Pre-Close phase begins at 15:00 AST. Orders accumulate for 10 minutes. At 15:10, a randomized uncross within 30 seconds determines the closing price. This closing price is the official price used for index calculations, NAV computations, and settlement.

- **Trade-at-Last:** After the closing auction uncross (15:10-15:20 AST), participants may execute orders only at the closing auction price. This session provides additional liquidity at the established closing price.

- **Volatility Auction (Interruption):** When a security price reaches the +/-10% static price limit, continuous trading halts and a 5-minute call auction is initiated. The auction price becomes the new reference price, after which continuous trading resumes.

### 3.2 Continuous Trading
- **Type:** Order-driven market
- **Priority:** Price-time priority (best price first, then earliest entry time at the same price)
- **Session:** 10:00 - 15:00 AST (5 hours)
- **Matching:** Continuous automatic matching via the X-Stream INET engine

### 3.3 Price Discovery
- **Opening price:** Determined by single-price auction algorithm maximizing tradable volume at the uncross
- **Closing price:** Determined by closing auction uncross; if no closing auction trade occurs, the last traded price during continuous trading is used [unverified]
- **Reference price:** Previous session's closing auction price; serves as the baseline for daily price limits
- **Randomized uncross:** Both open and close uncross times are randomized within 30 seconds to prevent manipulation and enhance price integrity

## 4. Order Types

### 4.1 Standard Order Types

| Order Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Limit Order | Buy or sell at a specified price or better |
| Market Order | Execute immediately at the best available price |

### 4.2 Advanced Order Types

| Order Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Stop Order | Triggered when a pre-set price level is reached [unverified â availability may be broker-dependent] |
| Auction Order | Participates only in opening or closing auctions |

### 4.3 Time-in-Force Options

| TIF | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| DAY | Valid for the current trading session only |
| IOC | Immediate or Cancel â fill what is possible, cancel remainder |
| FOK | Fill or Kill â execute in full or cancel entirely |

*Note: Detailed order type specifications and full TIF options should be confirmed from official Tadawul Trading and Membership Procedures.*

### 4.4 Order Modification / Cancellation
- Orders can be modified or cancelled during Pre-Open and Continuous Trading sessions
- Modifications that change price or increase quantity lose time priority
- During Non-Cancel (uncross) periods, cancellations are not permitted

### System History

| Period | System | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Pre-2001 | Manual trading | Paper-based, broker-mediated transactions |
| 2001-2008 | Tadawul Electronic System | First electronic trading, clearing, and settlement system; launched October 16, 2001 |
| 2008-2015 | SAXESS (Nasdaq OMX) | Nasdaq OMX trading platform; upgraded Tadawul's capacity significantly |
| 2015-present | X-Stream INET (Nasdaq) | World's fastest multi-asset trading engine at the time; first in Middle East; 40K orders/sec, <40 microsecond latency |

### Technology Stack
- Nasdaq X-Stream INET platform for order matching and execution
- Nasdaq post-trade technology for clearing and settlement (via Muqassa, the CCP subsidiary)
- Nasdaq Surveillance (SMARTS) for market surveillance [unverified]
- Market data dissemination infrastructure supporting real-time and delayed feeds

## 6. Market Data

### 6.1 Data Feed Protocols

| Protocol | Description | Use Case |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Market Data Feed (MDF) | Direct exchange feed sourced from Tadawul | Real-time and delayed market data |
| ICE Consolidated Feed | Third-party normalized data via ICE | Global distribution, multi-exchange consolidation |

### 6.2 Data Levels
- **Best Price (Level 1):** Last sale price, best bid and offer
- **Market Depth (Level 2):** Best five bid and offer prices and quantities
- **Premium (Full Depth):** Complete order book depth via dedicated channels

### 6.3 Distribution Infrastructure
- Direct exchange feeds available to licensed data vendors and members
- Third-party redistribution through global vendors (Bloomberg, Refinitiv, ICE, etc.)

### 6.4 Historical Data
- Historical price and trading data available through the Saudi Exchange website and licensed data providers

## 8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers

### 8.1 Price Limits

| Type | Threshold | Action |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Static Daily Price Limit | +/- 10% from reference price (previous close) | Orders beyond the limit are rejected; if price hits the limit, volatility interruption is triggered |

### 8.2 Circuit Breakers

| Level | Trigger | Halt Duration |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| Volatility Interruption (Individual Security) | Security price reaches +/- 10% static price limit | 5-minute call auction; auction price becomes new reference price; continuous trading resumes |
| Newly Listed Securities (Main Market) | +/- 10% limit applies for the first 3 trading days | 5-minute call auction upon trigger |
| Nomu â Parallel Market (All Securities) | +/- 10% limit on continuous basis | 5-minute call auction upon trigger |

**Note:** Market-wide circuit breakers (index-level halts) are not prominently documented in available sources. Individual security volatility interruptions are the primary mechanism. [unverified â confirm whether index-level circuit breakers exist]

### 8.3 Pre-trade Risk Controls
- **Fat-finger checks:** Orders beyond the daily price limit (+/- 10%) are automatically rejected
- **Order size limits:** Maximum order value and quantity limits set by brokers and the exchange [unverified â specific thresholds not confirmed]
- **Throttling:** Message rate controls likely enforced at the gateway level (consistent with X-Stream INET architecture) [unverified]

### 8.4 Kill Switch
- [unverified â kill switch capability not confirmed from available sources; expected as part of Nasdaq technology platform]

## 9. Regulatory Framework

### 9.1 Supervising Authority
- **Capital Market Authority (CMA)** â established in 2003 under the Capital Market Law (Royal Decree No. M/30, dated 2003)
- CMA is an independent government authority reporting directly to the Prime Minister
- Responsible for regulating and developing the Saudi capital market, protecting investors, and ensuring market fairness and transparency
- Website: https://cma.org.sa

### 9.2 Key Regulations

| Regulation | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Capital Market Law (2003) | Foundational legislation establishing CMA, authorizing the exchange, and setting framework for securities regulation |
| Rules for Foreign Investment in Securities | Governed foreign access via QFI regime (2015-2026); amended January 2026 to grant barrier-free access to all foreign investors |
| Listing Rules | Requirements for Main Market and Nomu listings; includes corporate governance, disclosure, and free float requirements |
| Market Conduct Regulations | Prohibitions on insider trading, market manipulation, and fraud |
| Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Terrorist Financing | Compliance requirements for all market participants |
| Corporate Governance Regulations | Board composition, audit committees, disclosure obligations for listed companies |
| ESG Disclosure Guidelines | Voluntary guidelines launched by Tadawul (2021); growing adoption with companies reporting ESG performance almost tripling since launch |

### 9.3 Market Surveillance
- CMA conducts market surveillance to detect insider trading, market manipulation, and other violations
- Nasdaq SMARTS surveillance technology utilized [unverified]
- Real-time monitoring of trading patterns, unusual price and volume movements
- CMA has enforcement powers including fines, trading suspensions, and criminal referrals

### 9.4 Reporting Requirements
- Listed companies must file annual and interim financial statements
- Material event disclosure requirements (continuous disclosure)
- Major shareholder notifications (5% threshold)
- ESG reporting increasingly encouraged (voluntary, with mandatory elements expected under Vision 2030 roadmap) [unverified]

### 9.5 Cross-border Arrangements

**Foreign Investor Access Evolution:**

| Year | Milestone |
|------|-----------|
| Pre-2015 | Foreign access only via swap agreements and P-Notes |
| 2015 | QFI program launched â institutional investors with USD 5 billion+ AUM |
| 2018 | QFI threshold lowered; ownership caps raised from 5% to 10% per investor |
| 2019 | Foreign Strategic Investor (FSI) framework introduced; MSCI EM and FTSE Russell EM inclusion completed |
| 2026 (Feb 1) | **QFI regime abolished** â all foreign investors granted barrier-free direct access through licensed Saudi intermediaries; swap agreement framework discontinued |

**Current Foreign Ownership Limits (as of February 2026):**
- 49% aggregate foreign ownership cap per listed company
- 10% cap per single foreign investor
- Foreign strategic investors subject to separate rules for ownership beyond standard limits

**Foreign Holdings:** Total foreign holding value reached SAR 443.78 billion (USD 118.34 billion) at the end of February 2026.

**MSCI EM Inclusion (2019):** Saudi Arabia was added to the MSCI Emerging Markets Index in a two-phase process (May and August 2019), significantly increasing passive and active foreign fund flows. QFI-owned holdings increased to SAR 134.48 billion in 2019. The inclusion was a key milestone under Vision 2030's Financial Sector Development Program.

*Sources: [Greenberg Traurig](https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2026/01/saudi-arabia-abolishes-qfi-status-and-opens-the-market-to-all-foreign-investors); [CMA announcement](https://cma.gov.sa/en/MediaCenter/NEWS/Pages/CMA_N_3974.aspx); [Bloomberg/Tadawul](https://sponsored.bloomberg.com/article/tadawul/saudi-stock-exchange-is-a-top-destination-for-foreign-equity-flows); [Latham & Watkins](https://www.lw.com/en/insights/saudi-cma-broadens-main-market-access-for-foreign-investors)*

## 11. Recent Developments

### System Upgrades (Last 5 Years)
- 2020: Introduction of closing auction mechanism and Trade-at-Last session
- 2020: Settlement cycle updated to T+2 to align with international standards
- 2025: Tick size band reform (effective June 29, 2025) â six-tier structure with lower minimums for sub-SAR 25 securities

### New Products / Segments
- **Derivatives:** SF30 Futures Index and ongoing development of equity derivatives; Saudi Exchange preparing new generation of debt and derivatives products
- **ESG:** ESG Disclosure Guidelines launched (2021); GCC Unified ESG Metrics (29 metrics) introduced 2023 under Tadawul chairmanship of GCC Exchanges Committee
- **ETFs:** Growing ETF market with new listings including Albilad MSCI Saudi Equity ETF (2025)
- **REITs:** Expanding REIT market supporting real estate sector development

### Regulatory Changes
- **February 2026:** QFI regime abolished; market fully opened to all foreign investor categories with barrier-free access
- **2025-2026:** CMA introduced new Instructions for Foreign Strategic Investors' Ownership, codifying 49% aggregate and 10% per-investor foreign ownership limits
- **2025:** Amendments to listing rules and tick sizes under FSDP roadmap

### Strategic Initiatives
- **Vision 2030 / FSDP alignment:** Ongoing reforms to deepen capital markets, increase market cap as percentage of GDP, and diversify the economy away from oil dependence
- **IPO pipeline:** ~40 IPO applications under CMA review at end of 2025, spanning energy, healthcare, financial services, real estate, mining, and technology
- **Offshore Securities Business License:** Launched to attract international intermediaries to operate in the Saudi market
- **Data as investment product:** Saudi Exchange investing in data services as a standalone revenue stream
